topics.topic: MigrationClosure identity and uniqueness across store histories and restores
questions: Are closures created by successful imports in different store histories distinct history-scoped facts, even when their recorded facts are equal, or are they the same value wherever those facts are equal?
Is the closure unique only in the current store history, or must audit subjects distinguish multiple closures that can arise over the lifetime of one Registry instance after restores?

When a backup containing a MigrationClosure is restored and thereby starts a new store history, is the restored closure the same value copied from the former history, or a distinct history-scoped closure—and, if distinct, what makes the store history part of its identity?

quotes: Substitution: there is at most one, and two records of "the migration succeeded at instant T" would mean the same thing. Continuity: it is written once and never changes; it is a fact about the store's history (R0-89), not a thing with a life.
None; absent, then present for the rest of the store's history. A store restored after a loss from a backup made before the import begins a history without it (R0-89).
Durable, at most one per store history (R0-89): an instance that restores a store from before the import may import again, and that history then holds its own closure.
judgement.why: MigrationClosure is expressly a value, so equal recorded facts denote the same value, while uniqueness and import blocking are scoped to the current store history; separate histories may each hold a closure record without giving those records distinct entity identities.

topics.topic: Whether restore preserves the original closure transition or starts with the closure as initial state
questions: Does a restored store history inherit the backed-up history, including the original absent-to-present transition, or does it begin at restore with MigrationClosure already present as initial state?
